placements.why: The discussion articulates overarching governance principles and strict operational boundaries for managing a phased technical migration across multiple sites.
placements.title: operational containment and governance rules for multi-site rollouts
placements.frame: How does the organization structure, sequence, and isolate technical and operational risks during multi-site system cutovers?

placements.title: known, contained operational friction is prioritized over unbounded parallel cutover risk
placements.frame: Does this expression justify sequential rollouts and empirical soak intervals by prioritizing bounded operational friction over concurrent deployment risk?
placements.why: Establishes a firm sequencing thesis: sites cut over strictly one at a time with a mandatory two-week soak grounded in exception queue flattening, accepting contained local friction to avoid unbounded multi-site failure.

placements.title: reporting workloads are strictly isolated to replicas during high-load cutovers
placements.frame: Does this expression mandate strict infrastructure isolation to protect transactional production stability during critical migration windows?
placements.why: Establishes an absolute operational rule in the runbook requiring all analytical and reporting reads to hit read replicas during cutover windows to prevent live system outages.

placements.title: vendor remains the authoritative system of record until full programme cutover
placements.frame: Does this expression defend retaining a single external source of truth throughout a phased rollout to prevent reference data drift and cross-system accountability gaps?
placements.why: Establishes the policy that reference data ownership remains with the vendor until the final site cutover completes, avoiding multi-site drift and clear accountability boundaries.
